messages:
Emma: Hey team — ACME POC goes live tomorrow. They asked for a hosted API key that can handle short bursts up to 120 qps and a sustained ~60 qps for the first 2 weeks. Can we provision a scoped key with a 14d TTL and soft limits so we don’t risk impacting other customers?
Mike: Yep we can do that. Best practice is a scoped key with a named policy (poc/acme-2026), TTL=14d, IP allowlist if they want, and a soft rate limit override for the duration. We can also add a daily token cap.
Raj: +1. Two cautions: 1) If they run noisy end-to-end tests we should route their traffic to the low-cost model variant to avoid token-cost shock. 2) Add automated disable on surge error rate (>10%) so we don’t have a noisy-hosting incident.
Emma: Helpful. Can you give me the exact steps and a curl/cli snippet I can forward to ACME? They want self-serve instructions for IP allowlist and rotating keys.
Mike: Quick CLI example (internal tool):
```
# create scoped key with TTL, soft limits and ip allowlist
redwood keys create \
  --name poc-acme-2026 \
  --scope "poc:acme" \
  --expires 14d \
  --rate "burst=120,sustained=60" \
  --soft-limit true \
  --daily-cap 200000 \
  --ip-allowlist 198.51.100.0/24
```
And the curl for testing: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <SCOPED_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'`
Raj: Console path: Console > Keys > Scoped Keys > poc-acme-2026. There’s a toggle for auto-rotate and a manual revoke button. We’ll wire alerts to #incidents if error-rate threshold trips.
Emma: Can we make the soft limit send warning logs instead of immediate 429s for the first 24 hours? ACME is nervous about hard failures during the demo. :slightly_smiling_face:
Mike: We can set soft=true which will emit warning metrics and degrade to a throttled profile only if sustained breaches continue past 1h. For the first 24h we’ll keep it gentle.
Raj: Implementing a temporary silent-throttle for 24h window. If sustained breach after that then full enforcement. Also setting a hard safety cap at 250 qps (absolute) to protect the pool.
Emma: Great — can you add an item that we document billing note for the POC? ACME needs written note: POC usage billed at hosted POC rate, any sustained usage beyond caps will be billed normally.
Mike: Will confirm pricing with finance and drop the pricing line in the POC email.
Sara (ACME): Thanks — can you also include how to rotate keys mid-POC? We have multiple testers and want to rotate daily.
Raj: Rotation steps: Console > Keys > Scoped Keys > rotate key (creates new token, retains policy). You can also use `redwood keys rotate --name poc-acme-2026 --notify` to auto-send to webhook. Recommend 24h rotation and update IP list if needed.
Emma: I’ll send the instructions now. Mike — ping me once pricing is confirmed and Raj send the console link.
deploy-bot: policy update applied to key poc-acme-2026 by raj — TTL set to 14d, soft-limit=true, burst=120,sustained=60
Mike: Confirmed — finance approved the POC rate; will share single-line billing note for the email.
Emma: Thanks all, sending to ACME now. :thumbsup:
